newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAB SAYS TO EXPAND IN CURRENT MARKETS.
newsitem.headline: SAB SAYS TO EXPAND IN CURRENT MARKETS.

text.p: Drinks giant South African Breweries Ltd said on Thursday that any cash from a possible share issue of up to two billion rand would be used in overseas markets it already had a presence in, not entering new regions.

"We have determined our markets and we have entered those markets and we would be continuing our expansion in those geographical areas," group corporate finance and development director Malcolm Wyman told Reuters.

Earlier in a brief statement the group said it would explore the possibility of issuing for cash ordinary shares worth up to five percent of the existing issued ordinary and automatically convertible preference shares.

Wyman said the group would embark on a three week roadshow of investors to test the waters on the idea, before deciding whether to go ahead with it. "At this stage we are conducting roadshows, rather than raising money," he said
But analysts have hailed the plan and say it will be received positively, making it look an almost certainty.

SAB, with brand names like Castle and Lion, dominates its home beer market with a 97 percent market share. In order to grow, it has expanded rapidly into other African states and further afield into Europe and China.
"There is no secret that part of our startegy is to expand our beer business internationally," Wyman said.

SAB has bought controlling stakes in the state breweries of Tanzania, Zambia and Mozambique and is negotiating to buy Angola's. It has also established itself in Hungary, Romania and, most recently, Poland.
The firm also has 55 percent of the Shenyang brewery in north east China.
Wyman said SAB would use the cash to fund projects in all three of its target areas of eastern and central Europe, China and Africa.
"We would be looking to use cash in all three, but primarily Europe and China," he said.
